reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch read "man of war" in 16:18 as an inference from David's lion-and-bear exploits, not evidence of prior battlefield service.

discrepancy.note: Paine flagged 1 Samuel 16 and 17 as two contradictory accounts of how Saul and David first became acquainted.

quotes.text: I observed two chapters in I Samuel (xvi. and xvii.) that contradict each other with respect to David, and the manner he became acquainted with Saul; as Jeremiah xxxvii. and xxxviii. contradict each other with respect to the cause of Jeremiah's imprisonment.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), note on 1 Samuel 16 and 17.

sides.snippet: Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, who is skillful in playing, and a mighty man of valor, and a man of war, and prudent in speech, and a comely person; and Yahweh is with him.
sides.verseText: Then answered one of the young men, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, who is skillful in playing, and a mighty man of valor, and a man of war, and prudent in speech, and a comely person; and Yahweh is with him.

sides.snippet: You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for you are but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
sides.verseText: Saul said to David, You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for you are but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
